A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OrthoRank study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–I are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original token-sink analyses, benchmark results, throughput measurements, ablations, and appendix experiments and generation examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results on C4, zero-shot tasks, LongBench, and TruthfulQA, together with the main-text and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 revises the reported generation procedure: v1 uses a threshold derived from prefill-selected tokens, whereas v2 describes selecting tokens by a fixed-ratio ranking against accumulated context. The orthogonality criterion, selective-layer approach, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain WikiText-2 analysis and calibration, C4 evaluation, the five zero-shot tasks, LongBench, TruthfulQA, and the appendix generation example. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: SLEB, Shortened LLaMA without fine-tuning, the Figure 6 comparators, and the token-selection comparison sets are unchanged. The newly cited Bae et al. work is not added to any reported experiment.

E3.justification: The experimental implementation description in Section 4.1 replaces prefill-derived thresholding during generation with accumulated-context ranking at the fixed selection ratio. This is a reported testing-procedure revision; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun. Other settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The selection-criterion, normalization, KV-computation, and sparsity ablations are unchanged. The appendix similarity analyses, layerwise comparisons, dynamic-ratio experiments, and generation case study are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Run and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including Section 4.1's statement that throughput is averaged over 50. No seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples are retained. For example, Table 1 still reports C4 perplexity of 8.74 for SLEB+OrthoRank on Llama-2-13B at 20% sparsity. Appendix result tables and generation outputs are identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical observations, token-importance definition, and Equations (1)–(15) are unchanged, including Appendix C's gradient derivation and RMS-scaling assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about token-sink alignment, training-free orthogonality-based selection, and performance relative to layer pruning.

C2.justification: Mechanistic explanations, result interpretations, and applicability qualifications are unchanged. These include Section 3.2's restrictions on suitable layers and Appendix G's recommendation to use sparsity below 40%.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the explicit prefill-threshold implementation description with an accumulated-context ranking description for generation. Hardware, batch size, model configurations, selection ratios, and appendix implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bae et al. (2023), 'Fast and robust early-exiting framework for autoregressive language models with synchronized parallel decoding,' to the introduction, related work, and bibliography. The broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to the generation explanation in Section 4.1, the added citation, and the version/date stamp. Section organization and the remaining narrative, including all appendices, are unchanged.

P2.justification: The edits produce local text-spacing and reference-layout changes. Figures and tables retain their content, structure, captions, and placement; the appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The added early-exit reference modestly improves citation coverage. However, Section 4.1 substitutes a different generation-selection rule without explaining whether this corrects documentation or changes the implementation behind the unchanged results. Its effect on reproducibility and evidential support is therefore unclear, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
